cons: • This is a non-binding resolution expressing opinion only — it does not change any law or require any action, so its practical impact on election security is minimal.
• Recognizing photo ID as a 'fundamental component' of secure elections could be cited to support stricter voter ID laws that may disproportionately affect elderly, low-income, and minority voters.

pros: • Reaffirms U.S. sovereignty by stating that the United States is not subject to International Criminal Court (ICC) jurisdiction, protecting American service members and officials from foreign prosecution.
• Provides clear policy guidance for U.S. diplomats and international partners on America's position regarding the ICC.
cons: • Strains diplomatic relations with allied nations that are ICC members and support international accountability for war crimes and genocide.
• May be seen as undermining global efforts to hold human rights violators accountable, reducing U.S. moral authority on international justice issues.

pros: • Ensures the Intelligence Committee has operational funding.
• Supports congressional oversight of intelligence activities.
cons: • Authorizes spending without substantive policy debate.
• Lacks transparency on how funds will be allocated.

pros: • Honors a pivotal moment in the civil rights movement.
• Educates the public on the Greensboro Four's courage.
cons: • Non-binding resolution with no legislative impact.
• Congressional time could address substantive civil rights bills.

pros: • Recognizes the important role of tribal colleges.
• Raises awareness of educational opportunities for Native students.
cons: • Non-binding resolution with no funding attached.
• Week designations have minimal practical impact.

pros: • Addresses animal-related issues under the Agriculture Committee's jurisdiction and oversight.
• Likely targets fighting or mistreatment of animals, strengthening cruelty prevention laws.
cons: • Federal animal fighting laws already exist, so this may duplicate current enforcement efforts.
• Could impose new reporting requirements on farmers and animal owners.

pros: • Provides unique ZIP Codes for specific communities, improving mail delivery accuracy.
• Helps remote or underserved communities gain better postal service and address recognition.
cons: • Requires USPS administrative resources that could be used for more pressing operational needs.
• Very narrow in scope, benefiting only a few specific communities rather than the general public.

pros: • Enhances retail security on military bases, protecting service members and their families.
• Deters theft and crime on military installations where law enforcement resources are limited.
cons: • Imposes new security requirements on military base retail operations, increasing costs.
• May create burdensome regulations for small businesses operating on military installations.

pros: • Supports NASA rocket engine testing, advancing space exploration and technology development.
• Maintains U.S. leadership in aerospace by preserving critical testing infrastructure.
cons: • Adds federal spending for space programs when domestic priorities like healthcare need funding.
• Benefits specific testing facilities but may not address broader NASA funding shortfalls.

pros: • Expands historic preservation tax credits, encouraging restoration of older buildings.
• Creates jobs in construction and revitalizes historic downtowns and communities.
cons: • Reduces federal tax revenue at a time of high deficits and national debt concerns.
• Primarily benefits real estate developers rather than local residents or small businesses.

pros: • Extends incentive payments for accountable care organizations through 2027, encouraging coordinated care.
• Helps lower healthcare costs by rewarding providers for quality rather than quantity of services.
cons: • Extends a costly Medicare incentive program without proven long-term savings results.
• May benefit large hospital systems more than small independent physicians and rural providers.

pros: • Addresses housing and community development issues to improve safety and stability.
• Targets shoreline or environmental risks that threaten coastal housing communities.
cons: • May impose new federal regulations on coastal property development and land use.
• Could face implementation challenges due to varying state and local shoreline laws.

pros: • Aims to reduce wildfire risk through active forest management and hazardous fuel reduction.
• Streamlines environmental reviews to accelerate forest restoration and thinning projects.
cons: • Expedited environmental reviews could bypass important ecological protections.
• Active logging under the guise of forest health may harm sensitive wildlife habitats.

pros: • Supports domestic critical mineral and rare earth element production for U.S. supply chains.
• Reduces reliance on foreign adversaries for minerals needed in defense and technology.
cons: • Mining operations could cause environmental damage to sensitive public lands and watersheds.
• Mining projects face long permitting timelines and local opposition that may delay benefits.

pros: • Protects the Buffalo Tract area from development, preserving natural landscapes and habitats.
• Supports conservation efforts and maintains public access for recreation on federal lands.
cons: • Removes land from potential economic uses like energy development, mining, or grazing.
• May conflict with local communities that rely on public lands for resource-based livelihoods.

pros: • Allows reporting of positive rental and utility payments to credit bureaus, helping consumers build credit.
• Expands credit access to millions of Americans who lack traditional credit history.
cons: • Could incentivize landlords to report negative payment data, damaging tenants' credit scores.
• May increase data accuracy concerns as more non-traditional data enters credit reporting.

pros: • Provides federal resources and support for victims of gun violence and their families.
• Funds community-based programs to address trauma and prevent future gun violence.
cons: • Increases federal spending without addressing root causes like mental health or policing.
• May overlap with existing state and local victim assistance programs, creating duplication.

pros: • Limits credit reporting agencies from selling mortgage pre-approval data to marketers.

• Reduces the size of the federal bureaucracy and potentially saves taxpayer money.
cons: • The ATF plays a crucial role in enforcing federal firearms laws, combating gun trafficking, and investigating explosives-related crimes.
• Abolishing the ATF without a replacement agency could create gaps in federal law enforcement that impact public safety.

pros: • Creates a select committee focused on electoral reform, which could address concerns about voting access, election security, and campaign finance.
• A dedicated committee allows Congress to study election issues in depth and develop bipartisan reform proposals.
cons: • Select committees can become partisan battlegrounds rather than productive reform vehicles.
• Could duplicate the work of existing committees like House Administration that already oversee elections.

pros: • Protects pets and animals from harm by strengthening penalties for animal cruelty or improving animal welfare standards.
• Addresses growing public concern about animal welfare and pet safety.
cons: • Federal animal welfare legislation may overlap with existing state laws, creating enforcement confusion.
• Could impose regulatory burdens on pet owners, breeders, or animal businesses.

pros: • Named after Laken Riley, this bill strengthens immigration enforcement by requiring detention of undocumented immigrants charged with certain crimes.
• Aims to prevent violent crimes by ensuring individuals accused of theft and other offenses are held pending proceedings.
cons: • Mandatory detention could lead to overcrowding in immigration facilities and increase costs for the immigration system.
• May apply to individuals who have not been convicted of a crime, raising due process concerns.

pros: • Ensures women veterans have access to contraception through the VA, addressing a specific healthcare need for the growing female veteran population.
• Improves comprehensive healthcare for veterans by covering reproductive health services.
cons: • May increase VA healthcare costs that need to be funded through additional appropriations.
• Some argue contraception coverage should be handled through private insurance rather than the VA system.

pros: • Addresses a specific healthcare gap for women veterans by improving menopause care through the VA healthcare system.
• Recognizes that the veteran population is increasingly female and requires targeted healthcare services.
cons: • Expanding VA healthcare services for specific conditions requires additional funding that may not be appropriated.
• Could create an uneven standard of care between male and female veterans for gender-specific health issues.

pros: • Helps disabled veterans afford housing by providing additional support and benefits, addressing homelessness and housing instability among veterans.
• Recognizes the sacrifices of disabled veterans by ensuring they have access to stable, accessible housing.
cons: • Housing support programs require sustained federal funding that may not be guaranteed in future budgets.
• Could overlap with existing VA housing assistance programs, creating administrative complexity.

pros: • Provides dental care benefits to veterans through the VA, addressing a significant gap in current veteran healthcare coverage.
• Dental health is linked to overall health — poor dental care can lead to serious medical conditions.
cons: • Adding dental benefits to VA healthcare would require substantial new funding that Congress would need to appropriate.
• Could increase wait times for other VA medical services if resources are stretched.

pros: • Reserves a low bill number for the Speaker's future use on a priority legislative item.
• Follows the traditional practice of setting aside numbers for leadership's legislative agenda.
cons: • Contains no substantive policy content until the Speaker designates a bill for this number.
• The reservation process can delay which policy proposals receive early bill numbers.

pros: • Reserves a low bill number for the Minority Leader's future legislative proposals.
• Maintains the tradition of reserving early numbers for minority party priority legislation.
cons: • Is a procedural placeholder with no actual policy language or impact.
• Delays the assignment of this number to substantive legislation that could advance through Congress.

pros: • Reserves an early bill number for the Speaker's major legislative initiative.
• Follows longstanding congressional tradition of leadership priority numbering.
cons: • Is a procedural placeholder with no text or policy substance until filled.
• Multiple reserved Speaker slots can suggest leadership control over the legislative agenda.

pros: • Reserves a bill number for the Minority Leader's future policy proposals.
• Helps ensure minority party priorities receive low-numbered visibility.
cons: • Contains no legislative content and has no direct impact on policy.
• The placeholder system can inflate the public perception of how many bills are actively being considered.

pros: • Supports restoration of oyster reefs, which improves coastal ecosystems, water quality, and fish habitat.
• Could benefit coastal communities through job creation in restoration and increased seafood production.
cons: • Does not specify a funding source or authorization level for the recovery programs it establishes.
• Oyster restoration projects can be costly and slow, with uncertain long-term survival rates for restored reefs.

pros: • Rescinds unobligated IRS enforcement funds, redirecting taxpayer money away from what critics call over-aggressive auditing.
• Uses the savings for an emergency crisis fund, potentially addressing urgent national needs more directly.
cons: • Cutting IRS enforcement funding could reduce the agency's ability to collect taxes owed, potentially increasing the federal deficit.
• The bill does not specify which crisis or exigent need the redirected funds would address.

pros: • Modifies tax sourcing rules so income from U.S. territories like Puerto Rico and Guam is treated more fairly.
• Could stimulate economic growth in U.S. territories by reducing tax barriers for businesses operating there.
cons: • Changes to territorial sourcing rules could reduce federal tax revenue without offsetting spending cuts.
• May create new tax planning opportunities that allow mainland corporations to shift income to territories.

pros: • Provides technical and financial assistance for groundwater recharge projects, addressing critical water shortage issues in drought-prone western states.
• Modifies the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to repurpose unobligated Bureau of Reclamation funds for water infrastructure.
cons: • Repurposing unobligated balances from previous legislation may reduce funding for the originally intended water projects.
• The bill focuses on Bureau of Reclamation areas and does not address groundwater issues in other parts of the country.

pros: • Aims to create fairer tax treatment for U.S. territories compared to the 50 states and the District of Columbia.
• Could help businesses and residents in territories like Puerto Rico by reducing tax complexity and inequities.
cons: • The bill lacks a detailed summary making it difficult to assess its full fiscal impact on federal revenue.
• Prior territorial tax parity proposals have faced opposition over concerns about revenue loss and tax avoidance.

pros: • Prohibits federal Title X family planning grants from going to entities that perform abortions or fund other providers that do.
• Aligns federal funding with the policy that taxpayer dollars should not support abortion services.
cons: • Could reduce access to family planning services, including contraception and cancer screenings, at clinics that currently receive Title X funds.
• Would force some health clinics to choose between providing comprehensive reproductive care and losing federal funding.

pros: • Prohibits state and local governments from establishing firearm registration or licensing requirements, protecting Second Amendment rights.
• Creates a uniform national standard for firearm regulations, preventing a patchwork of different state rules.
cons: • Would override state and local gun safety laws that many communities have chosen to enact through their own democratic processes.
• Eliminating registration and licensing requirements removes tools that law enforcement uses to track firearms used in crimes.

pros: • Establishes technical and procedural standards for AI-generated and prerecorded telephone messages, targeting the growing problem of AI robocalls.
• Provides clear statutory authority for regulating AI voice systems that can impersonate real people in phone calls.
cons: • Setting technology-specific standards may quickly become outdated as AI voice technology evolves.
• Enforcement of robocall regulations has historically been difficult, even with statutory authority in place.

pros: • Expands tax deductions for floor plan financing interest on travel trailers and campers, putting them on equal footing with other recreational vehicles.
• Could support the RV and camping industry by reducing the financing costs for dealers who stock travel trailers.
cons: • Reduces federal tax revenue by expanding business interest deduction eligibility without offsetting spending cuts.
• Primarily benefits recreational vehicle dealers rather than individual consumers or broader economic growth.

pros: • Requires the U.S. flag to be flown at its highest peak on Inauguration Day each year, honoring the peaceful transfer of power.
• Provides clear statutory guidance for flag display on this specific national occasion.
cons: • Current flag code already gives the President authority to order flags at full staff on Inauguration Day, making this bill largely duplicative.
• Focusing on a symbolic measure may distract from more substantive governance issues that need congressional attention.

pros: • Establishes a House committee to identify underperforming or nonessential federal programs, pursuing government efficiency.
• Could identify significant taxpayer savings by systematically reviewing programs for potential elimination or reform.
cons: • Creates a new committee with additional congressional resources rather than having existing committees perform this oversight.
• Previous government efficiency initiatives have frequently identified waste but struggled to achieve actual elimination of programs.

pros: • Prohibits the Federal Highway Administration from establishing cordon pricing for New York City's Central Business District Tolling Program.
• Protects motorists from paying congestion pricing fees to enter Manhattan, preventing what supporters call a new tax on drivers.
cons: • Would override a local transportation policy that New York State and City approved to reduce traffic congestion and fund transit improvements.
• Could increase traffic congestion, air pollution, and commute times by removing the financial incentive to use alternative transportation.

pros: • Prohibits the FHWA from including congestion pricing in federal value pricing pilot programs, protecting drivers from tolls on existing free roads.
• Preserves free access to highways that were built with taxpayer dollars and have historically been toll-free.
cons: • Limits state and local flexibility to use congestion pricing as a tool for managing traffic and funding road maintenance.
• Removes a proven transportation demand management tool that cities use to reduce gridlock and encourage public transit use.

pros: • Strengthens workers' rights to form unions and bargain collectively by reforming labor law provisions that critics say favor employers.
• Would impose penalties on employers who violate labor laws and expand protections for workers engaging in organizing activities.
cons: • Could increase costs for businesses by expanding union influence and making it harder to hire replacement workers during strikes.
• Would override state right-to-work laws, forcing workers in those states to pay union dues even if they choose not to join.

pros: • Requires the Department of Energy to report on its use of authority to waive nonfederal cost-sharing requirements for energy projects.
• Increases transparency and accountability for how the DOE uses taxpayer dollars in public-private energy partnerships.
cons: • Imposes new reporting requirements on DOE without changing the underlying policy on cost-share waivers.
• Falls short of actually limiting or reforming the DOE's authority to waive cost-sharing, instead just requiring an after-the-fact report.

pros: • Requires standardized procedures for reciprocal fire suppression cost share agreements between federal, state, and local governments.
• Ensures fire departments are fairly reimbursed when they assist in fighting fires on federal lands.
cons: • Creates new administrative requirements that could complicate rapid emergency response when quick mutual aid agreements are needed.
• Standardized federal procedures may not account for local differences in fire response costs and operations across different regions.

pros: • Lowers the voting age to 16, giving younger citizens a voice in elections that directly affect their education, environment, and future — issues like climate policy and student debt that have lifelong impacts.

• Research from countries like Austria and Scotland that lowered their voting age shows 16- and 17-year-olds vote at rates comparable to older first-time voters, and the habit of voting early can increase lifetime civic participation.
cons: • Amending the Constitution requires two-thirds of both chambers and three-fourths of states, making this a lengthy and difficult process with uncertain prospects that may distract Congress from other priorities.
• Critics argue that 16-year-olds may lack the life experience and maturity to make informed voting decisions on complex issues like taxation, foreign policy, and economic regulation.

pros: • Provides clearer legal standards for when separate securities law violations should be treated as a single violation for penalty purposes, reducing uncertainty for businesses facing SEC enforcement actions.
• Could prevent the SEC from stacking multiple penalties on a single course of conduct, making penalties more proportional to the actual wrongdoing.
cons: • Aggregating multiple violations into a single penalty could weaken deterrence by reducing the financial consequences for repeated or widespread securities law violations.
• May give sophisticated financial firms more leeway to push the boundaries of securities law knowing that multiple violations will be treated as one.

pros: • Makes permanent the VA's pilot program for accepting donations of property and facilities, allowing the VA to more efficiently expand its infrastructure through private and community contributions.
• Encourages community involvement in supporting veterans by giving organizations and individuals a clear path to donate buildings and land to the VA.
cons: • Accepting property donations could lead to the VA taking on facilities that are substandard or have high maintenance costs, shifting financial burdens from donors to taxpayers.
• Making the program permanent reduces congressional oversight, as a pilot program would otherwise require periodic review and reauthorization.

pros: • Expands VA health care to cover infertility treatments and fertility preservation for veterans with service-connected conditions that affect fertility, addressing a gap in care for those injured in service.
• Also covers the partners of covered veterans, recognizing that infertility affects families, not just individual service members, and helps veterans build families after their service.
cons: • Adding expensive fertility treatments like IVF to VA coverage could significantly increase the cost of veterans' health care without a clear budget offset.
• May create equity concerns among veterans, as those with service-connected infertility would receive a benefit not available to other veterans with different medical needs.

pros: • Establishes a bipartisan commission to study long-term fiscal challenges and recommend policies to reduce the national debt, bringing expert analysis to a persistent problem.
• Focuses on medium- and long-term fiscal sustainability, aiming to address structural deficits rather than short-term budget fluctuations.
cons: • Creates a new commission without giving it binding authority — past fiscal commissions have produced recommendations that were largely ignored by Congress.
• The study and recommendation process could take years, delaying any meaningful action on the growing national debt while producing advisory findings with no enforcement mechanism.

pros: • Requires the HUD Inspector General to testify annually before Congress, increasing oversight and accountability for how taxpayer dollars are spent on housing programs.
• Focuses specifically on fraud, waste, and abuse detection at HUD, which administers billions of dollars in housing assistance, helping ensure funds reach intended recipients.
cons: • The HUD Inspector General already provides regular reports to Congress — this bill mandates in-person testimony that adds a procedural requirement without necessarily improving oversight outcomes.
• Additional congressional testimony requirements consume time from both IG staff and congressional committees without guaranteed improvements in program performance.

pros: • Returns historic Cherokee lands in Monroe County, Tennessee — including the Sequoyah Museum and Chota Memorial — to the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, addressing a longstanding request from the tribe.
• Preserves culturally and historically significant sites for the Cherokee people by placing them into federal trust, ensuring their protection for future generations.
cons: • Taking land into federal trust removes it from the local property tax base, potentially reducing revenue for Monroe County services like schools and infrastructure.
• The bill addresses a specific land claim for one tribe in one county, setting a precedent for federal action on many similar tribal land claims that could have broad fiscal implications.

pros: • Creates a two-year window for clergy and Christian Science practitioners to revoke their exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes, giving them the flexibility to change their status if their financial circumstances change.
• Addresses a permanent decision that many clergy made decades ago, allowing them to opt into retirement and disability benefits they would otherwise be locked out of.
cons: • If large numbers of clergy opt into Social Security, it could reduce the system's overall revenue if the newly covered individuals tend to claim benefits for longer than they contribute.
• The two-year window is limited — clergy who miss the window would remain permanently locked out, which some might argue is still too restrictive.

pros: • Halts implementation of a BLM land management plan in Wyoming that critics argue imposes excessive federal restrictions on grazing, energy development, and other uses of public lands.
• Preserves local input and state-level decision-making over federal land management by preventing a controversial plan from taking effect before elected representatives can weigh in.
cons: • Blocking the BLM plan could delay responsible resource management on 780,000+ acres of public land, potentially leaving sensitive ecosystems and wildlife habitats without needed protections.
• Congress overriding a specific agency land management decision sets a precedent that could politicize routine land management choices traditionally handled by professional land managers.

pros: • Prohibits implementation of a BLM land use plan for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming that local communities and state officials argue restricts energy development and multiple-use access to public lands.
• Supports state sovereignty over federal land management decisions by preventing a top-down plan from taking effect without adequate local input.
cons: • The Buffalo Field Office manages over 780,000 acres of public lands — blocking the management plan leaves these lands without updated guidance for grazing, energy development, and conservation.
• Congressional intervention in a specific BLM planning decision could create uncertainty for all ongoing land management planning processes in other states and districts.

pros: • Extends drought-relief pilot projects in the Colorado River Basin through FY2026, continuing efforts to boost water levels in the Upper Basin and Lake Mead during the ongoing megadrought.
• Provides critical water conservation funding and programs to the seven Colorado River Basin states, which supply water to over 40 million people across the Southwest.
cons: • Extends existing pilot projects without providing new funding or expanded authority, meaning the same programs continue without addressing whether they are effectively conserving water.
• Does not address the fundamental challenge of overallocation in the Colorado River system, instead funding temporary measures while long-term agreements remain unresolved.

pros: • Raises the SALT deduction cap from $10,000 to $100,000 ($200,000 for joint filers), providing significant tax relief to homeowners in high-tax states like New York, California, and New Jersey.
• Eliminates the marriage penalty in the SALT deduction by doubling the cap for married couples, ensuring married taxpayers are not disadvantaged compared to single filers.
cons: • The SALT deduction primarily benefits high-income households in expensive coastal states — this large increase would overwhelmingly benefit the wealthiest taxpayers and add significantly to the federal deficit.
• Increasing the cap to $100,000 would cost an estimated hundreds of billions of dollars over a decade, requiring substantial spending cuts or revenue increases elsewhere to offset.

pros: • Allows disabled veterans to use HOV (carpool) lanes regardless of the number of passengers, reducing commute times for those who served their country and have service-connected disabilities.
• Gives public authorities clear statutory authority to extend HOV access to disabled veterans, removing legal uncertainty that might prevent states from offering this benefit.
cons: • Expanding HOV lane access to disabled veterans could increase congestion in HOV lanes, potentially reducing the incentive for carpooling and the lanes' effectiveness at reducing overall traffic.
• Requires a visible identification method (license plate or transponder), which could create privacy concerns or administrative burdens for both veterans and state DMVs.

pros: • Designates the Margaret Woodbury Strong Museum in Rochester as the National Museum of Play, giving it national recognition that could boost tourism and grant funding for the museum and the region.
• Recognizes the cultural and educational value of play in child development by elevating a major play-focused institution to national status.
cons: • The designation is largely symbolic — it does not provide federal funding for the museum or guarantee its long-term financial stability.

• Using the 'National Museum' designation for a pre-existing private museum that was not originally established as a federal institution could be seen as an honorary title with limited substantive impact.

pros: • Prohibits pay increases for teleworking federal employees who are not reporting in person, incentivizing a return to physical federal offices and potentially improving collaboration and service delivery.
• Could save taxpayer money by reducing the number of federal employees receiving locality-based pay adjustments while working remotely from lower-cost areas.
cons: • Penalizes teleworking employees regardless of their performance or productivity, ignoring the proven efficiency gains and work-life balance improvements from remote work.
• Could make it harder for the federal government to recruit and retain talent, especially in competitive job markets where remote work is a standard expectation in the private sector.

pros: • Allows AI and machine learning systems to be eligible to prescribe certain drugs, potentially expanding access to prescription medications in areas with provider shortages.
• Could reduce wait times and administrative burden on doctors by letting AI handle routine prescription renewals and standard medication management.
cons: • Allowing AI to prescribe drugs raises serious patient safety concerns — AI systems may miss clinical nuances, drug interactions, or patient-specific factors that a trained medical professional would catch.
• The regulatory framework for AI prescribing is not established, and this bill does not specify what qualifications, testing, or oversight would apply to AI prescribers.

pros: • Directs multiple federal agencies including the CIA, FBI, IRS, and Department of Defense to publicly disclose all records related to the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, advancing government transparency.
• Requires disclosure within 90 days, preventing further delays in releasing records that are already required by the 1992 JFK Records Act.
cons: • Most JFK assassination records have already been released — this bill may cover only a small number of remaining documents, some of which may be appropriately withheld for national security reasons.
• Forces disclosure of records from multiple agencies on an accelerated timeline without allowing for national security or privacy redactions that career intelligence professionals deem necessary.

pros: • Prevents states from setting a maximum workweek shorter than 60 hours for agricultural employees, providing farmers with flexibility in managing seasonal labor demands during planting and harvest.
• Establishes a uniform federal standard that preempts a patchwork of state laws, giving agricultural employers legal certainty across state lines.
cons: • Overrides state laws designed to protect farmworkers from excessive work hours — agricultural work is physically demanding and 60-hour weeks without overtime rules could lead to worker fatigue and safety issues.
• Preempting stronger state labor protections for agricultural workers could affect a workforce that is already among the most vulnerable and least protected under federal labor law.

pros: • Requires federal agencies to survey managers annually on their workplace experience, providing data to improve federal management practices and identify problems in agency operations.
• Mandates public release of survey results, increasing transparency about how well federal agencies are being managed.
cons: • Adds a new annual survey requirement on top of the existing Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey, creating additional administrative burden across all federal agencies without guaranteed improvements.
• Survey results may not capture meaningful management quality information and could be subject to manipulation or low response rates.

pros: • Requires federal grant applicants to certify they have not violated laws against bringing individuals into the U.S. illegally, ensuring federal funds do not support organizations involved in unlawful immigration practices.
• Provides a 10-year lookback period, creating a strong deterrent against past and future violations by entities seeking federal funding.
cons: • The certification requirement could be used to deny grants to legitimate organizations based on broad interpretations of the smuggling prohibition, potentially affecting faith-based and humanitarian groups providing aid to migrants.
• Creates additional paperwork and legal liability for grant applicants without clear evidence that current grant recipients are involved in immigration-related violations.

pros: • Raises the SALT deduction cap to $15,000 ($30,000 for joint filers), providing moderate tax relief to middle-class homeowners in high-tax states without the massive cost of a full repeal.
• Provides more targeted relief than the existing $10,000 cap, helping families who were hardest hit by the cap rather than the highest-income households.
cons: • Still primarily benefits homeowners in high-income, high-tax states rather than addressing broader tax fairness issues, and would reduce federal revenue by tens of billions of dollars.
• The $15,000 cap still leaves many homeowners in states with high property taxes unable to fully deduct their state and local taxes, so the relief is only partial.

pros: • Honors General Bernie Mittemeyer, a decorated veteran and former Army Surgeon General, by naming the Lubbock VA clinic after him, recognizing his service and contributions to military medicine.
• The naming is a community-driven recognition effort that comes at no additional cost to taxpayers.
cons: • Facility naming bills are ceremonial and do not improve veterans' health care services, expand clinic capacity, or reduce wait times for the veterans who use the facility.
• Congress spends time on naming legislation that could be handled at the local or administrative level, taking focus away from substantive veterans policy issues.

pros: • Prohibits selling Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil to entities headquartered in adversarial nations like Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea, protecting a critical national security asset.
• Ensures taxpayer-funded petroleum reserves do not benefit nations that pose a threat to U.S. interests or compete with American energy producers.
cons: • The Strategic Petroleum Reserve is typically sold through competitive bidding processes with strict end-user controls — it is unclear whether significant sales to these entities currently occur, meaning the bill may address a nonexistent problem.
• Restricting the pool of potential buyers could reduce competition and lower prices received for SPR oil, potentially costing taxpayers money in future sales.

pros: • Creates an advisory committee to oversee Amtrak's implementation of food and beverage service improvements, potentially enhancing the quality and variety of onboard dining options for passengers.
• Establishes internal review mechanisms to ensure Amtrak follows through on recommendations from its own Food and Beverage Working Group.
cons: • Creates a new advisory committee and internal review process without providing funding for actual food service improvements — better food requires investment, not just oversight.
• A narrow focus on dining service on a single rail operator raises questions about whether this is an appropriate use of federal legislation rather than an operational matter for Amtrak management.

pros: • Prohibits federal funds from going to entities that perform abortions (with exceptions for rape, incest, and medical emergencies), ensuring taxpayer dollars are not used for abortion services.
• Requires annual certification from grant recipients, creating ongoing accountability for how federal funds are spent in relation to abortion services.
cons: • Could restrict funding for hospitals, clinics, and health organizations that provide a wide range of reproductive health services beyond abortions, potentially limiting access to contraception and other care.
• The certification requirement adds administrative burden on health care providers and could lead to funding gaps for essential health services in underserved communities.

pros: • Requires DHS to reinstate the Migrant Protection Protocols (the 'Remain in Mexico' policy), which required asylum seekers to wait in Mexico while their claims were processed, deterring illegal border crossings.
• Could reduce the burden on U.S. immigration detention facilities and border processing resources by keeping asylum applicants south of the border during their proceedings.
cons: • Forces asylum seekers to wait in dangerous border cities in Mexico, where they face heightened risks of violence, kidnapping, and extortion while their claims are processed.
• Mexico must consent to accepting returned migrants — if Mexico refuses cooperation, DHS would be required to implement the policy without the necessary partner nation agreement.

pros: • Reauthorizes EPA's Long Island Sound programs through FY2029, continuing restoration and conservation efforts for one of the nation's most重要的 estuaries, which supports fishing, tourism, and recreation.
• Funds stewardship grants that support local conservation projects, helping towns and nonprofits restore coastal habitats and improve water quality.
cons: • Reauthorizes programs without specifying funding levels, meaning actual appropriations may not match the authorized amounts and programs could still be underfunded.
• Focuses narrowly on one specific estuary rather than addressing broader coastal restoration needs across the country.

pros: • Reauthorizes the Rural Innovation Stronger Economy (RISE) Grant Program, which supports job creation and economic development in rural areas that often lack access to capital and business development resources.
• Expands the program to include career pathway programs and industry partnerships, helping rural workers gain skills for better-paying jobs.
cons: • The reauthorization does not provide specific funding levels, so the program's impact depends on annual appropriations that may be lower than needed.
• Rural economic development programs have mixed track records — without clear performance metrics, it's difficult to know if RISE grants are producing lasting jobs and economic growth.

pros: • Allows states to observe daylight saving time year-round, ending the twice-yearly clock change that many Americans dislike and that studies show increases traffic accidents and health problems.
• States could choose the time system that works best for their geography and economy, providing flexibility rather than a one-size-fits-all federal mandate.
cons: • Without a federal uniform time standard, states could end up in different time zones at different times of year, creating confusion for interstate travel, commerce, broadcasting, and transportation.
• States that adopt permanent DST would have very late winter sunrises — for example, sunrise after 9:00 AM in northern states — which has been linked to health and safety concerns.

pros: • Allows all military retirees to receive their full military retired pay and veterans disability compensation simultaneously, ending the current offset that reduces retired pay for those with disability ratings under 50%.
• Eliminates what many veterans view as an unfair penalty on those with service-connected disabilities, ensuring they receive the full benefits they earned through military service.
cons: • Eliminating the offset for all disability ratings would cost billions of dollars over time, adding to federal spending without a corresponding revenue source or spending cut.

• The current law's 50% threshold already provides full concurrent receipt for those with more severe disabilities — this bill extends it to those with lower ratings, which could reduce incentives for accurate disability ratings.

pros: • Renames HSAs as 'Health Freedom Accounts' and increases contribution limits, making it easier for Americans to save tax-free for medical expenses and giving them more control over their health care spending.
• Expands the definition of qualified medical expenses to include direct primary care arrangements and health sharing ministry costs, broadening options for consumers.
cons: • Eliminates the exclusion from income for employer-provided health coverage exceeding a certain threshold, which could increase taxes on workers with generous employer-sponsored health plans.

• Higher HSA contribution limits and expanded definitions primarily benefit wealthier individuals who can afford to max out their accounts, doing little for the uninsured or those with limited incomes.

pros: • Requires DHS to suspend entry of migrants without valid documents whenever the agency cannot detain or return them — shifting the burden from U.S. communities to border entry points and enforcing existing immigration law.
• Creates a clear trigger (inability to detain or return) that activates enforcement measures, preventing 'catch and release' practices that supporters argue encourage illegal immigration.
cons: • Suspending entry for migrants without valid documents could overwhelm border ports of entry with processing backlogs, affecting legal trade and travel across the border.
• Could lead to migrants being stranded at the border without access to asylum procedures, potentially violating U.S. obligations under international refugee treaties.

pros: • Directs the IRS to compile lists of PPP loan recipients whose loans were forgiven but who did not withhold payroll taxes, helping identify potential fraud or abuse in the pandemic relief program.
• Increases transparency around the Paycheck Protection Program, which distributed over $800 billion with limited oversight, by requiring the IRS to track and report on loan recipients.
cons: • Many PPP loans were forgiven years ago — compiling lists of recipients' payroll tax withholding status may not recover significant funds and could create administrative burdens for the IRS.
• Some PPP borrowers may have valid reasons for not withholding payroll taxes (e.g., sole proprietors, independent contractors), so the data could be misleading without proper context.

pros: • Increases the maximum prison sentence for falsely claiming military awards for personal gain from one year to three years, providing stronger deterrence against stolen valor that dilutes the meaning of military honors.
• Protects the integrity of prestigious military awards like the Medal of Honor and Purple Heart, ensuring they remain meaningful symbols of sacrifice and bravery.
cons: • Stolen valor cases are relatively rare — increasing penalties addresses a small problem with disproportionately harsh sentencing that may not significantly deter fraudsters.
• Longer prison sentences will increase federal incarceration costs without necessarily addressing the underlying motivations for falsely claiming military honors.

pros: • Condemns Turkey's continued occupation of Cyprus and calls for troop withdrawal, taking a principled stand on a longstanding violation of international law that has divided the island for over 50 years.
• Urges President Trump to prioritize the Cyprus resolution in U.S. foreign policy, potentially leveraging American influence to push for a negotiated settlement.
cons: • As a non-binding resolution, this expresses the sense of the House but does not require any action from the executive branch or impose consequences on Turkey.
• Could strain diplomatic relations with Turkey, a NATO ally, at a time when cooperation on broader security issues in the region may be more strategically important.

pros: • Calls for the return of the Parthenon Marbles to Greece, supporting cultural heritage repatriation and acknowledging the controversy over how these artifacts were removed from Greece in the early 19th century.
• Adds U.S. congressional weight to Greece's longstanding request, potentially influencing the United Kingdom to enter negotiations.
cons: • As a non-binding resolution, this has no force of law and does not require any action by the United Kingdom or any U.S. government agency.
• Addresses a cultural dispute between Greece and the United Kingdom — a matter in which the U.S. Congress has no direct jurisdiction or role.

pros: • Expresses the sense of the House that it should not adjourn until all annual appropriations bills are enacted, applying political pressure on Congress to complete its most basic funding responsibility on time.
• Could help prevent government shutdowns and stopgap continuing resolutions by signaling that members should stay in session until the budget is done.
cons: • As a sense-of-the-House resolution, it is non-binding and has no enforcement mechanism — members can vote for it and then proceed to adjourn without consequence.
• Keeping the House in session without a deadline mechanism could lead to stays that produce no results, as has happened in past appropriations standoffs.

pros: • Fills vacancies on key House committees (Appropriations, Energy and Commerce, Financial Services, Ways and Means), ensuring these important panels have the membership needed to conduct business and consider legislation.
• Allows both parties to place their members on the committees where they can be most effective, reflecting the normal organizational work of Congress at the start of a session.
cons: • This is a routine administrative resolution with no substantive policy impact — it simply assigns members to committees as is standard operating procedure.
• Committee assignments are typically negotiated by party leadership behind closed doors, so this resolution merely formalizes decisions already made.

pros: • Authorizes proxy voting for new parents in the House of Representatives, allowing members who have recently given birth or whose spouse has given birth to vote on legislation without being physically present on the floor.
• Modernizes congressional rules to accommodate the realities of pregnancy and new parenthood, potentially encouraging more young parents and women with families to serve in Congress.
cons: • Proxy voting in the House is a significant departure from the traditional requirement that members be physically present to vote, which some argue undermines accountability and the deliberative process.

• The resolution applies only to new parents and pregnant members, creating a special voting accommodation for one category while other members with serious medical conditions or emergencies cannot vote remotely.

pros: • Allows committee chairs to approve remote witness testimony without requiring a committee vote on each request, making it easier for expert witnesses with scheduling conflicts or distance limitations to testify before Congress.
• Brings real-world experience and diverse perspectives to congressional hearings by reducing barriers to participation for witnesses who cannot travel to Washington.
cons: • Eliminating the committee vote requirement for remote testimony reduces the deliberative check on when witnesses can appear remotely, potentially allowing chairs to bypass objections from ranking members.
• Remote testimony may reduce the effectiveness of committee oversight by making it harder for members to engage with witnesses and assess their credibility in person.
